modules.title: 源 HTML 怎样变成运行时 DOM 树
当前页面为什么会和源文件不同

items.title: 浏览器先解析文档
items.text: 浏览器读取 HTML，把文档中的元素、文字和属性组织成节点之间的层级关系，页面据此开始渲染。

items.title: 脚本可以修改这棵树
items.text: 点击按钮后，JavaScript 可以创建、删除或修改节点，所以 Elements 面板里的 DOM 可能已经不同于最初的 HTML 文件。

modules.title: 容易混淆的地方
modules.text: DOM 是浏览器当前页面的运行时文档树，不是初始 HTML 文件，也不是数据库。脚本把任务插入 DOM 后，刷新页面可能消失；要跨刷新、设备或用户保留，仍需另行保存数据。现代前端框架（如 React、Vue）帮你管理 DOM 更新——你描述界面应该长什么样，框架自动算出哪些节点需要变化。AI 生成的 React 代码里很少出现 document.createElement，因为框架在背后替你操作这棵树。

lessonPractice.title: 点击“新增”后页面多出任务，但查看源代码时没有这条任务。下一步应怎样判断？

options.label: 检查运行时 DOM 和脚本，确认新节点是怎样被创建并插入页面的
options.feedback: 对。查看源代码反映初始文档，Elements 面板里的运行时 DOM 才能显示点击后的节点变化。

options.label: 直接把这条任务写进初始 HTML，保证页面一开始就能看到
options.feedback: 这会把一次点击产生的动态内容变成固定内容，仍然没有解释脚本怎样更新当前页面。

options.label: 把页面多出的任务当成已保存数据，直接检查数据库记录
options.feedback: DOM 更新只证明当前页面有了节点，不证明数据已写入数据库；刷新后是否保留还要单独验证。

en.title: A task appears after clicking Add, but it is missing from View Source. What should you determine next?

options.label: Inspect the runtime DOM and script to see how the new node was created and inserted
options.feedback: Correct. View Source shows the initial document; the runtime DOM in Elements shows the node change after the click.

options.label: Write the task into the initial HTML so it is visible from the start
options.feedback: That turns click-generated content into fixed content and still does not explain how the script updates the current page.

options.label: Treat the new task as saved data and inspect the database record directly
options.feedback: A DOM update proves only that the current page has a node. It does not prove a database write; refresh persistence needs a separate check.

lessonAgentPrompt.title: 你可以这样告诉 AI Agent
lessonAgentPrompt.text: 请检查点击“新增”后运行时 DOM 是否插入了任务节点，并说明是哪段脚本完成的。再刷新页面确认这只是 DOM 更新还是已经持久保存；不要把当前页面出现节点当成数据库写入证据。

en.title: You can say this to an AI Agent
en.text: After clicking Add, inspect whether the runtime DOM contains the new task node and identify which script inserted it. Then refresh to determine whether this was only a DOM update or was persisted. Do not treat a visible node as proof of a database write.

learning.assumes: You have seen page source and encountered new content or elements appearing after a click.
learning.outcome: You can inspect the runtime DOM and script when the current page differs from initial HTML, and distinguish a page update from persisted data.

modules.title: How source HTML becomes the runtime DOM tree
Why the current page can differ from the source file

items.title: The browser parses the document first
items.text: The browser reads HTML and organizes its elements, text, and attributes into a hierarchy of nodes that begins the page render.

items.title: A script can change the tree
items.text: After a click, JavaScript can create, remove, or change nodes, so the DOM in Elements may differ from the original HTML file.

modules.title: What it is not
modules.text: The DOM is the browser's current runtime document tree, not the initial HTML file and not a database. A task inserted into the DOM may disappear on refresh; retaining it across refreshes, devices, or users requires separate data storage. Modern frontend frameworks (like React or Vue) help manage DOM updates—you describe what the interface should look like, and the framework automatically calculates which nodes need to change. AI-generated React code rarely uses `document.createElement`, because the framework manipulates this tree behind the scenes for you.

distinctions.label: HTML
distinctions.text: {c:html} is the document source that describes the initial structure; {c:dom} is the browser's current node tree after parsing and runtime changes.

distinctions.label: Browser storage
distinctions.text: {c:dom} changes what the current page shows; {c:browser-storage} is a separate mechanism for keeping data in the browser across page loads.
